slides.title: Four nonprofits go to court
body: Public Citizen, Heat Initiative, The Alliance for Secure AI and Irreplaceable Education Fund filed a **63-page complaint** on Thursday in San Francisco. It names OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, Meta and SpaceXSI, Elon Musk's AI unit at SpaceX.

slides.title: Make today's AI the limit
body: The plaintiffs want an injunction barring the five from developing or deploying AI **more capable than their best systems** as of the filing date. That would not necessarily shut down ChatGPT, Claude or Gemini.

slides.title: No AI-led AI research
body: The complaint also asks the court to stop the companies from using AI to run or direct research into better models, known as **recursive self-improvement**.

slides.title: Existing law, public nuisance
body: The plaintiffs invoke California's **Unfair Competition Law** and argue that building ever more capable AI is a public nuisance. Public Citizen's Robert Weissman says the suit asks the court to apply existing law.

slides.title: Allegations, not findings
body: **Defendants have not been found liable**, and warnings about catastrophe do not automatically establish a violation of California law. Meta declined to comment; the others did not respond at first. On Saturday, PauseAI held a march in Berlin.

sources.title: OpenAI, Anthropic, Google and Other AI Giants Face Lawsuit Demanding Development Freeze
Coalition of Nonprofits Files Landmark Lawsuit to Stop Development of Advanced AI Systems at Anthropic, Google, Meta, OpenAI, and SpaceXSI that Proliferate Bioweapons and Cyberattacks

facts.text: Irreplaceable Education Fund, Public Citizen, Heat Initiative and The Alliance for Secure AI filed a lawsuit in the Superior Court of California, County of San Francisco, seeking to freeze the development of increasingly advanced AI models at Anthropic, Google, Meta, OpenAI and SpaceXSI.
The 63-page complaint, filed Thursday in San Francisco Superior Court, targets 5 defendants (OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, Meta and SpaceX); the plaintiffs are 4 nonprofits.
SpaceXSI is Elon Musk's AI division at SpaceX, into which xAI has merged.
The plaintiffs ask for an immediate injunction forbidding the defendants from developing or deploying AI systems more capable than their most capable systems as of the date of the complaint.
That wouldn't necessarily mean shutting down ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini, or other existing products; it would effectively make today's technology the limit.
The complaint also asks the court to prohibit the companies from using AI to independently conduct or direct research into better models, a process related to recursive self-improvement.
The lawsuit invokes California's Unfair Competition Law, and one part of the argument is that developing increasingly capable AI systems creates a public nuisance.
Robert Weissman, co-president of Public Citizen, said the lawsuit asks the court to apply existing law and find the AI corporations' reckless practices unlawful and freeze further AI development.
As defendants they have not been found liable, and warnings about potential catastrophe do not automatically establish a violation of California law.
Meta declined to comment; the other defendant companies did not initially respond.
On Saturday, PauseAI held an AI Treaty March in Berlin as part of a worldwide day of action, urging an international agreement to contain AI risks.

caption:
Four nonprofits are asking a San Francisco court to freeze AI at today's level at OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, Meta and SpaceXSI.

These are the plaintiffs' allegations and requests. Defendants have not been found liable.

→ The 63-page complaint, filed Thursday, asks for an injunction against building or deploying AI more capable than the defendants' best systems as of filing
→ It also asks to bar AI-led research into better AI (recursive self-improvement)
→ The plaintiffs rely on California's Unfair Competition Law and a public-nuisance argument

Should courts have a say in how fast AI advances?
